messages:
Maya: Heads up — nightly builder snapshot (builder-2026-03-17) started failing our flash-attn fused kernel link on linux-x86. Saw this in CI for the paged-attn matrix job.

Chris: Ugh, saw the alert. Can you paste the linker error?

Maya: Sure, root job: https://ci.internal/build/3847 (short log below)

CI-Bot: build/eng-runtime/flash-paged: job failed (exit 2) — tail: `ld: undefined reference to 'flash_paged_kernel_v2'`

Maya: Full snippet: 
```
/usr/bin/ld: ./.libs/libflashkernel.a(paged.o): in function `paged_run':
paged.c:(.text+0x1f3): undefined reference to `flash_paged_kernel_v2'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

Jordana: That symbol is from the fused-flash variant we build with -DUSE_FUSED_KERNEL. Any change in toolchain can flip symbol mangling/versioning.

Chris: Last good build used gcc 12.5 + glibc 2.35 in the builder image. New snapshot bumped to gcc 13.2 and glibc 2.36. I'm suspecting LTO or visibility defaults.

Ellie: Also noticed our wheel build script strips symbols with `strip -s` as a final step for size. That can drop local linkage info for PIC objects if flags differ.

Maya: Reproducer I ran locally with the builder image: `docker run --rm -it redwood/builder:snapshot-2026-03-17 /bin/bash` then `make -C runtime/flashattn clean && make -j8`. Error is deterministic.

Chris: Two quick checks: 1) Is `-fvisibility=hidden` used? 2) Are we mixing `-flto` objects built with different compilers?

Maya: We do set `-fvisibility=hidden` in the shared lib build. LTO is enabled only for the optimized wheel pipeline, but the snapshot turned on `-flto=thin` by default in the distro GCC wrapper.

Jordana: If LTO is on, objects compiled with different GCC versions are ABI-unsafe. That could explain missing symbol at link-time if the symbol got optimized away or internalized.

Chris: Quick workaround: add `-fno-lto` to our build flags in CI until we pin toolchain. Also for the fused kernel we can add `extern \"C\" __attribute__((visibility(\"default\")))` to the kernel entry to avoid being hidden by visibility/LTO.

Ellie: Agreed. I'll open a tiny patch to explicitly export the symbol and add a CI guard to disable LTO in the ephemeral builder snapshots.

Maya: Another oddity — the container base changed from `debian:bookworm-slim` to `debian:bookworm-2026-snapshot` which carries a custom linker script. That can change symbol resolution order.

Chris: Noted. We should also audit the dockerfile and pin the builder base image hash in our release pipeline. Unpinned base images are risky for kernel-level stuff.

CI-Bot: Created ticket #IR-1092: "flash-attn: builder snapshot LTO/toolchain mismatch causing link failures" — assigned to @Ellie, @Chris.

Ellie: I'll push two CI changes: (1) add `-fno-lto` to the ephemeral build variant, (2) add an integration test that links fused and paged kernels into the shared lib with the snapshot image.

Maya: For long term, we should add a small static-check step in the packaging pipeline that runs `readelf -Ws` on the generated .so and asserts the kernel symbol is present. That would catch regressions early.

Jordana: Good call. Also let's update docs: note that builder snapshots can change `gcc` defaults and `strip` behavior. Put a checkbox in the kernel packaging guide to verify symbol export and LTO flags.

Chris: One more gotcha we hit in the last run: manylinux wheel build accidentally used host `ld.gold` rather than `ld.bfd` due to PATH ordering in the new image. gold has different behaviour for relocations. Might add that to the checklist.

Maya: OK, patch + CI guard is working locally for me. Will upload a minimal reproducer + patch in PR: https://git.internal/r/flash-attn/patches/2387

Ellie: Thx — I'll wire the ticket and monitor the next snapshot run. :thumbsup:

Chris: If anyone hits a similar failure, drop the short log here and ping me. We'll prioritize until pinned builder image lands.

Maya: Thanks all.
